hints.content:
$\displaystyle \int_{-5}^{-2} h(x) \,dx$ is the net area between the curve $y=h(x)$ and the $x$-axis between $x=-5$ and $x=-2$.

![The graph of function h has the region between the curve and the x-axis, between x = negative 5 and x = negative 2, shaded. The portion of the curve at the top of the shaded region is concave down, moving upward from (negative 5, 0) to (negative 2, 3).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/5f4588b27fa4c19615048a7d9b7be283de3e6e78)

Since the curve is $\blueD{\text{above}}$ the $x$-axis in this interval, the area is $\blueD{\text{positive}}$.

We can find this area using geometric area formulas. We have a quarter of a circle whose radius is $\goldD{3}$.

The area of the entire circle is $\pi\cdot \goldD{3}^2=9\pi$, and a quarter of that is $\dfrac{9\pi}{4}$.
